extracted.intended_audience: Nonprofit organizations (staff and board members) in Nebraska and Western Iowa; nonprofit leaders responsible for advocacy, compliance, communications, and governance.
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance and compliance checklist for nonprofit organizations engaging in public policy, advocacy, and lobbying activities, with regional (NE/IA) and federal legal references and best practices for communications, media relations, training, and expense tracking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage in public policy and advocacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Nonprofit organizations should engage in public policy and advocacy activities to promote constituent, organizational and sector interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocacy is framed as a central role nonprofits play in democratic participation; organizations are encouraged to use policy engagement as a tool for social change and to focus on promoting the common good.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote broad public participation and assist the public
rubrics_metrics.description: Nonprofits should work to promote broad public participation in public policy and advocacy efforts and should provide assistance to the public in these efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide resources, training, and support that help constituents participate in policy-making (e.g., voter encouragement, civic engagement assistance). Encourage and enable constituent voices rather than substituting for them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of Advocacy activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Include 'Advocacy' as an assessment item when evaluating organizational practice in public policy engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use as a category to review whether the organization is actively engaging in advocacy, what forms it takes, and how it aligns with mission and constituents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of Lobbying activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Include 'Lobbying' as an assessment item to determine whether advocacy expenditures and activities constitute lobbying and how they are managed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether communications are direct or grassroots lobbying, whether they refer to specific legislation, and whether grassroots communications include a call to action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify and maintain Resources for advocacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Include 'Resources' as an assessment item—ensure the organization has appropriate tools, training, staff, and materials to conduct advocacy and comply with rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resources include staff roles (e.g., media specialist), training programs, policy alerts subscriptions, and media contact databases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider 501(h) election when conducting lobbying
rubrics_metrics.description: If conducting any lobbying, consider making the 501(h) election under Internal Revenue Code §501(c)(3) and §501(h).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 501(h) expenditure test provides specific dollar limits as a percentage of the exempt budget (contrast with the vague 'no substantial part' test); form F5768 is the simple election form. Evaluate whether 501(h) suits the organization's lobbying plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with lobbying reporting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Comply with federal and state lobbying reporting requirements (e.g., Lobbying Disclosure Act of 1995; Neb. Rev. Stat. §49-1483.03; Iowa Code §68B.37; IRS Form 990 reporting).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish procedures to determine when reporting triggers apply, gather required information, and file disclosure reports timely. Track who is lobbying, topics, and expenditures for reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with prohibition on supporting/opposing candidates
rubrics_metrics.description: Comply with the prohibition on supporting or opposing candidates or elected officials under Internal Revenue Code §501(c)(3) and IRS Form 990 guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure activities, public statements, and communications do not cross the legal line into candidate support or opposition. Provide training and written policies for staff and board to prevent prohibited political campaign activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with prohibition on using federal funds to lobby
rubrics_metrics.description: Comply with restrictions on the use of federal funds for lobbying (see Office of Management & Budget Circular A-122 and Form 990 guidance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separate federally funded programs/activities from lobbying; establish accounting practices and procedures to ensure federal dollars are not used impermissibly for lobbying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal lobbyist registration when applicable
rubrics_metrics.description: Register under federal lobbyist registration rules (Lobbying Disclosure Act of 1995; 2 U.S.C. §1605) if you have lobbyists engaging at the federal level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine whether employees or contracted advocates meet the definition of lobbyists for registration and reporting; complete registration and periodic reports as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: State lobbyist registration (Iowa) when applicable
rubrics_metrics.description: If you have lobbyists in Iowa, comply with Iowa Code §68B.36 registration requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify state-specific triggers for registration, deadlines, and reporting content for Iowa; ensure local compliance procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: State lobbyist registration (Nebraska) when applicable
rubrics_metrics.description: If you have lobbyists in Nebraska, comply with Neb. Rev. Stat. §49-1480.01 (and related statutes) for registration and reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify Nebraska registration triggers and reporting obligations; integrate state compliance into overall tracking systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand that nonprofits may support or oppose legislation (within limits)
rubrics_metrics.description: Nonprofits may support or oppose legislation subject to lobbying limitations under IRC §501(c)(3)/§501(h) and Form 990 rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocacy for or against legislation is permissible but must be tracked and limited per expenditure tests or 'substantial part' standards; choose appropriate compliance path and document activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures to track lobbying expenses for reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish procedures to track lobbying expenses to meet reporting and expenditure-limit requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain accounting codes, documentation, time tracking, and expense allocation methods to calculate lobbying expenditures accurately for 501(h) tests and disclosure filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide stakeholders with nonpartisan resources and training
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide stakeholders with nonpartisan resources and training on issues important to your constituencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep materials neutral in partisan terms; focus on education about issues, processes, and how constituents can engage; offer training that clarifies boundaries between advocacy and prohibited political activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subscribe to policy alerts and stay current
rubrics_metrics.description: Subscribe to online policy alerts to keep abreast of current policy trends, issues and action needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use alerts to inform strategy, prepare rapid responses, and keep staff/board informed of legislative developments that affect constituents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage in regular peer conversation about legislative/social environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Engage in regular conversation with colleagues regarding the legislative and social environment to maintain awareness of trends and activities impacting constituents or mission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Share intelligence with peers, discuss coalition opportunities, and review potential implications for programming and advocacy; make this part of routine organizational dialogue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embed advocacy discussion into board and staff meetings
rubrics_metrics.description: Build discussion regarding advocacy and issues awareness into meetings at the board and staff level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regular agenda items keep leadership aware and accountable; use meetings to review policy priorities, compliance status, and constituent outreach plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide lobbying and advocacy training for staff and board
rubrics_metrics.description: Participate in good training related to lobbying and advocacy; ensure staff and board members understand opportunities, responsibilities and restrictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training should cover legal limits (candidate activity, federal/state lobbying rules), internal procedures, and practical communication practices; document completion and provide refresher sessions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid allowing fear or misinformation to limit advocacy work
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not allow fear or misinformation to limit the work you do on behalf of your constituents and mission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use correct information, legal guidance, and training to confidently pursue permissible advocacy; consult legal counsel as needed rather than defaulting to over-caution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage constituents to be advocates and assist civic engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Encourage constituents to vote and make their opinions known; assist constituencies in public and civic engagement at local, state and federal levels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support constituent-led advocacy (which may be less restricted than organizational lobbying in some contexts), provide tools for civic participation, and ensure nonpartisan framing where required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop a media specialist role and professionalize media output
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop a media specialist on staff to handle media releases, op-eds, and public service announcements; correctly format and submit materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign responsibility for media relations, and invest time in database-building, understanding outlet focus areas and deadlines, and producing professionally formatted materials to increase visibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Build and maintain a local media database and relationships
rubrics_metrics.description: Spend time developing a database of local media, know their focus areas and deadlines, and identify the right contact in each outlet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Periodic outreach (meetings, background briefings) and providing useful, non-promotional data will build trust and increase coverage of issues important to your mission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish yourself as a resource for media and policymakers
rubrics_metrics.description: Position the organization as a reliable resource by sharing data, background, story leads, and by meeting periodically with reporters, editors, policymakers and community leaders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on helping media with breaking stories and offering substantive background; build relationships over time—trust and time are the basis for effective policy and media relationships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct vs grassroots lobbying requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize the difference: direct lobbying communicates with policy makers; grassroots lobbying engages the public. Both must refer to specific legislation and express the organization’s view; grassroots communications must include a call to action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When planning communications, label and document whether activities are direct or grassroots lobbying, ensure references to specific legislation are explicit, and include clear calls to action for grassroots efforts so they are properly categorized and tracked.
